text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.6% today to $136.27, continuing a steep two-week decline of 9.6% that began right after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th. The stock has shed nearly $18 per barrel of equivalent value since late October, with most of the drop happening after earnings hit the market. While oil prices themselves remain relatively stable—US crude at $99.64 and global crude at $107.03—the company-specific earnings announcement appears to have triggered selling pressure that has dominated the recent moves.

The broader context shaping the selloff involves shifting political winds around energy. A Democratic sweep in the midterm elections and the associated backlash against fossil fuel expansion is creating headwinds for oil and gas majors, even as Middle East tensions with Iran theoretically support oil prices. Investors may be repricing the company for a lower long-term growth scenario in a political environment less favorable to new fossil fuel development.
